header.contentArea: Applied surgical science and critical care
guidelineVersions: NICE CG141 (updated Aug 2016, minor changes Mar 2025)

brief.scenario: Mr Derek Hollis, 67, vomited blood twice this morning and has passed black stool since last night. He takes naproxen for osteoarthritis and aspirin 75 mg daily after a stroke. He hasn't fainted. He has no known liver disease or heart failure. Pulse 104, BP 104/66.
brief.task: The examiner will ask about your assessment and management, giving results as you ask.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Resuscitate, score the risk, correct clotting, and get the right endoscopy at the right time.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Starting a PPI before endoscopy, or transfusing to a 'normal' haemoglobin.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "ABCDE, two large-bore cannulas, bloods including crossmatch, then I'll calculate his Glasgow-Blatchford score."

grid.label: Assessment and resuscitation
grid.fail: Starts with a PPI infusion and waits for bloods.
grid.pass: ABCDE; observations with NEWS2; two large-bore cannulas; FBC, U&E, LFT, clotting, crossmatch; IV fluids.
grid.high: If unstable, a 500 ml crystalloid bolus in under 15 minutes, reassess; critical care review if instability persists.

grid.label: Glasgow-Blatchford score
grid.fail: Can't name a pre-endoscopy score, or uses Rockall before endoscopy.
grid.pass: Calculates the Glasgow-Blatchford score at presentation; full Rockall after endoscopy.
grid.high: Works it aloud: urea 4, haemoglobin 3, systolic 1, pulse 1, melaena 1: total 10, high risk.

grid.label: Disposition and endoscopy timing
grid.fail: Plans an outpatient endoscopy, or doesn't say when.
grid.pass: Admits him; endoscopy within 24 hours of admission; immediately after resuscitation if unstable with severe bleeding.
grid.high: Knows NICE considers early discharge only at GBS 0; the BSG bundle considers outpatient care at GBS 1 or less.

grid.label: Red cell transfusion
grid.fail: Transfuses to a normal haemoglobin, or not at all when he's bleeding heavily.
grid.pass: Restrictive: transfuse below 70 g/L, target 70–100 g/L; higher trigger in ischaemic heart disease or instability.
grid.high: Says over-transfusion may be as harmful as under-transfusion; massive bleeding follows the major haemorrhage protocol instead.

grid.label: Clotting and anticoagulants
grid.fail: Gives platelets or plasma with normal results, or doesn't know when they are needed.
grid.pass: Actively bleeding: platelets if under 50, FFP if PT or APTT over 1.5 times normal, PCC for warfarin.
grid.high: Cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen stays under 1.5 g/L; life-threatening GI bleed on apixaban or rivaroxaban: involves haematology (NICE TA697 lists andexanet; BSH 2026: thrombotic risks appear to outweigh benefits).

grid.label: PPI, NSAIDs and aspirin
grid.fail: Starts a PPI before endoscopy and stops all antiplatelets indefinitely.
grid.pass: No PPI before endoscopy; PPI after endoscopy if stigmata of recent haemorrhage; stop naproxen.
grid.high: Continues low-dose aspirin for his stroke once haemostasis is achieved.

grid.label: Suspected variceal bleeding
grid.fail: Gives a PPI and nothing else to a patient with cirrhosis.
grid.pass: Suspected variceal bleed: terlipressin and prophylactic antibiotics at presentation; band ligation at endoscopy.
grid.high: Gives the bundle dose (terlipressin 2 mg IV four times a day), with caution in ischaemic heart or peripheral vascular disease.

grid.label: Re-bleed and escalation (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Keeps him on the ward waiting for the morning list.
grid.pass: Unstable re-bleed: major haemorrhage protocol, resuscitate, immediate endoscopy; tells registrar, endoscopist and critical care.
grid.high: Plans ahead: repeat endoscopy for re-bleeding; if unstable after endoscopic treatment, interventional radiology, or surgery if IR isn't promptly available.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you manage Mr Hollis?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd start an omeprazole infusion straight away and wait for his bloods.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The Rockall score, now, before endoscopy.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: He could go home and come back for an outpatient OGD.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd give two units to get him above 130.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd give FFP and a pool of platelets anyway, to be safe.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Overnight he vomits blood again; BP 82/50.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll ask the endoscopist to add him to tomorrow's list.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How would you manage Mr Hollis?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: ABCDE, observations with NEWS2, two large-bore cannulas; FBC, U&E, LFTs, clotting and crossmatch; IV fluids.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The Glasgow-Blatchford score now; the full Rockall score after endoscopy.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Urea 11.2, Hb 112. When should he be scoped?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: His score is high, so he's admitted, with endoscopy within 24 hours of admission.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I wouldn't transfuse at 112. Restrictive: transfuse below 70, aiming for 70 to 100.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Those are normal, so nothing now. If he were actively bleeding, platelets under 50; FFP only if his clotting times were over 1.5 times normal.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No PPI before endoscopy; a PPI afterwards if there are stigmata of recent bleeding. I'd stop the naproxen.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Then variceal bleeding is possible: terlipressin and antibiotics now, and band ligation at endoscopy.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Overnight he vomits blood again; BP 82/50.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Major haemorrhage protocol, resuscitate, and endoscopy immediately after resuscitation. I'd call my registrar, the endoscopist and critical care.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would you manage Mr Hollis?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: ABCDE and NEWS2. He's tachycardic, so two large-bore cannulas, bloods with clotting and crossmatch, and a 500 ml crystalloid bolus in under 15 minutes if he becomes unstable, then reassess.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Glasgow-Blatchford at presentation, Rockall after endoscopy.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Urea 11.2, Hb 112. When should he be scoped?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Blatchford: urea 11.2 scores 4, male haemoglobin 112 scores 3, systolic 104 scores 1, pulse 104 scores 1, melaena 1. Total 10, high risk.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Admit, endoscopy within 24 hours. NICE would consider discharge only at 0; the BSG bundle at 1 or less. He's nowhere near.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No transfusion at 112: trigger 70, target 70 to 100. Over-transfusion can be as harmful as under-transfusion, unless he bleeds massively.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Normal, so no platelets or plasma. If actively bleeding: platelets under 50; FFP only for clotting over 1.5 times normal, cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen stays under 1.5. If he were on apixaban with a life-threatening bleed, I'd involve haematology: NICE lists andexanet alfa for GI bleeds, but the BSH now advises caution because of thrombosis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No PPI before endoscopy. Stop the naproxen. Continue his aspirin once haemostasis is achieved, because it's protecting him from another stroke.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: His Blatchford would be 12, with 2 for liver disease. Terlipressin 2 mg IV four times a day, watching for cardiac or peripheral ischaemia, and IV antibiotics now; band ligation at endoscopy.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Overnight he vomits blood again; BP 82/50.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Major haemorrhage protocol and immediate endoscopy after resuscitation; critical care now. If he re-bleeds after endoscopic treatment and stays unstable, interventional radiology, or surgery if IR isn't available promptly.

failures.move: Leaving an unstable re-bleed for the next day's list.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: he can exsanguinate; unstable patients need endoscopy immediately after resuscitation.

failures.move: Treating a known cirrhotic with a PPI alone.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: variceal bleeding without terlipressin and antibiotics carries higher re-bleeding and death rates.
NICE advises against it for suspected non-variceal bleeding; it delays nothing useful and doesn't replace endoscopy.
Over-transfusion may be as damaging as under-transfusion.

recovery.when: You can't remember the score bands
recovery.line: I'd calculate the Glasgow-Blatchford score from his urea, haemoglobin, BP, pulse and presentation; a score above 0 means admission by NICE, above 1 by the BSG bundle.
Correction: no PPI before endoscopy; a PPI afterwards if there are stigmata.

knowledge.fact: Blatchford at first assessment, full Rockall after endoscopy; consider early discharge at Blatchford 0.
Blatchford bands: urea 10.0–24.9 scores 4; male Hb 100–119 scores 3; systolic 100–109 scores 1; pulse 100 or more 1; melaena 1; syncope, liver disease, cardiac failure 2 each.
Endoscopy immediately after resuscitation if unstable; within 24 hours for everyone else.
Restrictive transfusion: trigger Hb under 70 g/L, target 70–100 g/L. Outpatient care at GBS 1 or less.
Suspected variceal bleed: terlipressin and prophylactic antibiotics at presentation; band ligation for oesophageal varices.
BSH (2026): the risks of andexanet alfa appear to outweigh its benefits; involve haematology.

recall.think: Exsanguination, especially from varices or a re-bleeding ulcer.
recall.say: "Glasgow-Blatchford 10: high risk. Admit, endoscopy within 24 hours, sooner if unstable."
do: No PPI before endoscopy; terlipressin if varices

numbers.meaning: Blatchford for early discharge (NICE) / outpatient care (BSG)

recall.trap: A normal-looking haemoglobin early on; it lags behind the bleed.
recall.finish: Endoscopic haemostasis; interventional radiology or surgery for re-bleeding.

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format: 9 minutes with 1 minute's reading; examiner-led questioning in applied knowledge stations

sources.name: NICE CG141: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management
sources.version: Published 13 June 2012; last updated 25 August 2016; minor changes March 2025
sources.supports: Blatchford score at first assessment and full Rockall score after endoscopy (1.1.1); consider early discharge with pre-endoscopy Blatchford 0 (1.1.2); massive bleeding: blood, platelets and clotting factors per local protocol (1.2.1); over-transfusion may be as damaging as under-transfusion (1.2.2); platelets if actively bleeding and count under 50 x 10^9/L (1.2.4); FFP if actively bleeding and PT (or INR) or APTT over 1.5 times normal; cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen stays under 1.5 g/L (1.2.4); PCC for patients on warfarin who are actively bleeding (1.2.5); DOAC reversal per MHRA list; andexanet alfa per TA697 (1.2.8); endoscopy immediately after resuscitation if unstable with severe bleeding (1.3.1); within 24 hours of admission for all others (1.3.2); no PPI or H2RA before endoscopy for suspected non-variceal bleeding (1.4.3); PPI if stigmata of recent haemorrhage at endoscopy (1.4.4); repeat endoscopy for re-bleeding (1.4.6); interventional radiology for unstable re-bleeding after endoscopic treatment, or urgent surgery if not promptly available (1.4.7); terlipressin at presentation for suspected variceal bleeding (1.5.1); prophylactic antibiotics at presentation for suspected or confirmed variceal bleeding (1.5.2); band ligation for oesophageal varices (1.5.3); continue low-dose aspirin once haemostasis is achieved (1.6.1); stop other NSAIDs (1.6.2)

sources.name: Siau K, Hearnshaw S, Stanley AJ, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG)-led multisociety consensus care bundle for the early clinical management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Frontline Gastroenterol 2020;11(4):311-323
sources.supports: Observations with a validated early warning score such as NEWS; IV fluids for all, unstable patients a 500 ml crystalloid bolus in under 15 minutes; restrictive red cell transfusion: trigger Hb under 70 g/L, target 70-100 g/L, higher trigger in ischaemic heart disease or haemodynamic instability; critical care review for ongoing instability; GBS at presentation; consider outpatient management if GBS 1 or less; IV terlipressin 2 mg four times a day and IV antibiotics for suspected variceal bleeding; interrupt warfarin and DOACs at presentation; endoscopy within 24 hours, earlier after resuscitation if unstable; high-dose PPI after endoscopy for high-risk ulcer stigmata

sources.name: Blatchford O, Murray WR, Blatchford M. A risk score to predict need for treatment for upper-gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Lancet 2000;356:1318-21
sources.supports: Glasgow-Blatchford score: urea (mmol/L) 6.5-7.9 = 2, 8.0-9.9 = 3, 10.0-24.9 = 4, 25 or more = 6; haemoglobin men 120-129 g/L = 1, 100-119 = 3, under 100 = 6; women 100-119 = 1, under 100 = 6; systolic BP 100-109 = 1, 90-99 = 2, under 90 = 3; pulse 100 or more = 1; melaena = 1; syncope = 2; hepatic disease = 2; cardiac failure = 2

sources.name: NICE TA697: Andexanet alfa for reversing anticoagulation from apixaban or rivaroxaban
sources.supports: Andexanet alfa recommended for life-threatening or uncontrolled bleeding on apixaban or rivaroxaban only if the bleed is in the gastrointestinal tract (1.1)

sources.name: Buka RJ, et al. Use of andexanet alfa: a British Society for Haematology position statement. Br J Haematol 2026;208:1939–41
sources.supports: Risks of andexanet alfa appear to outweigh benefits for factor Xa inhibitor-associated bleeding

partner.opening: Mr Hollis has just been referred to you. How would you assess and manage him?

reveals.finding: Pulse 104, BP 104/66, RR 20, SpO2 97% on air, temperature 36.8°C, alert. Melaena on rectal examination. No signs of chronic liver disease.
Hb 112 g/L, urea 11.2 mmol/L, creatinine 96 µmol/L, platelets 236 x 10^9/L, INR 1.1, APTT normal.
Say: "Suppose he had alcohol-related cirrhosis." (He has none in this case; this tests the variceal pathway.)
Overnight: further haematemesis. Pulse 128, BP 82/50, Hb 74 g/L.

push.question: Would you start a PPI now?
push.expect: No: not before endoscopy for suspected non-variceal bleeding; after endoscopy if stigmata.

push.question: When would you transfuse him?
push.expect: Hb under 70 g/L, target 70–100; higher trigger if ischaemic heart disease or unstable; massive bleeding follows the major haemorrhage protocol.

curveballs.prompt: He is on warfarin, INR 3.8, and still bleeding.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop warfarin and give prothrombin complex concentrate because he is actively bleeding; involve haematology.

curveballs.prompt: A 24-year-old with one small haematemesis after retching, normal observations and bloods: Blatchford 0.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Consider early discharge with outpatient follow-up and clear safety-netting.

curveballs.prompt: After two endoscopic treatments he re-bleeds and is unstable.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Interventional radiology for embolisation; urgent surgery if IR isn't promptly available.
